description: Basic-knowledge client proposed COMPLEX structured note that requires no minimum knowledge (R1 passes) — R7 hard fail → UNSUITABLE. Tests: complexity gate triggers independent of knowledge requirement.
client_narrative: Ana Popescu is 44 years old and works as an administrative coordinator at a university. She earns approximately 48,000 euros per year and holds 50,000 euros in liquid savings. She wants to invest 15,000 euros for 5 years to supplement her long-term savings. Ana has basic investment knowledge: she has bought equity mutual funds through her bank on a few occasions but has never evaluated complex structured products. She rates her risk tolerance at 4 out of 10 — moderately risk-aware — and has confirmed she cannot afford to lose her investment. Her investment objective is moderate portfolio growth.
product_narrative: The product is a capital-at-risk structured note that provides conditional coupon payments linked to the performance of a basket of European equity indices. Coupons are paid only if all index levels remain above a predefined barrier on specified observation dates; if any index closes below the barrier at maturity, the investor receives a reduced capital repayment proportional to the worst-performing index. The note is classified as a complex financial instrument under MiFID II, publishes a KID, uses no leverage, and has a minimum recommended holding period of two years. Although the product itself does not specify a minimum knowledge level in its terms, the complexity of the payoff structure and barrier mechanics means it is categorised as COMPLEX.
